title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Separating the Task from the Model — Maxime Rivest & Isaac Miller
talk_summary: A DSPy talk arguing that repeated AI tasks should be defined as functions with a fixed contract (natural-language spec, code-enforced constraints, and evals), so the model, prompt, and harness become swappable implementation details. The claimed payoff is cheaper implementations via model swapping and automatic optimization, plus the ability to try new techniques without changing integrations.

takeaways.technique: Three-part task contract: spec + code constraints + evals
takeaways.what_they_do: Define each repeated AI task by (1) natural-language instructions/signature, (2) hard constraints enforced in code (retry with more reasoning, throw to human on invalid output), and (3) example-based evals for the long tail; then optimize inside that boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have the specs, the code, and the evals. And now, your goal is fully specified.

takeaways.technique: Swap models behind a fixed task interface
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the task boundary is fixed, the model is configured independently at the top of the program; you can move from an expensive model to a cheap one while keeping the same evals and business logic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They're able to do that because they went from an expensive model to a cheap model, but they could keep the same eval's

takeaways.technique: Escalating retry: cheap pass then reasoning pass
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a vanilla predict first; if the output fails a code check, rerun the same task with chain-of-thought, and throw to a human if a hard constraint (e.g. negative value) is violated.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if my first simple vanilla program doesn't extract my taxes, I want you to rerun with more reasoning

takeaways.technique: Treat repeated agent workflows as versioned functions
takeaways.what_they_do: Package a repeated AI task (e.g. spec+repo -> PR) as a named, reusable, composable unit with a fixed input/output contract, so internals (prompt, tools, loops) can change without breaking callers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can give it a spec, a repository, and you get a PR. Those are repeatable tasks.

takeaways.technique: Recursive language models for long context
takeaways.what_they_do: A technique for long-context tasks where the model recursively decomposes/handles context; exposed as a one-line swap in DSPy so the task signature stays constant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Recursive language models are a way to solve some kinds of long context programs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of hand-building datasets, use real traces, user actions, and product analytics as textual feedback that models convert into evals and a hill to climb, refining over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as you get more feedback from production, it's traces, it's user actions, it's product analytics
